headline: Dollar Heads for Fourth Week of Gains Following Anthropic IPO
author: Melos Ambaye

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- The dollar is headed for a fourth straight weekly gain as demand tied to the Anthropic PBC IPO further lifts the currency that has been supported by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and elevated US Treasury yields.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index is up 0.7% this week — on track for its longest winning weekly streak since Oct. 9. The advance comes as artificial intelligence lab Anthropic shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday. The biggest-ever public debut created more demand for the dollar as investors across the globe converted their currency to buy shares in the company. Anthropic stock jumped 17% on its first day of trading.

"A fair estimate of foreign take-up of the IPO is probably in the $10 billion to $15 billion range," Brent Donnelly, president of Spectra Markets, wrote in a note Thursday. "Those US dollar buyers are racing against corporates who are trying to get their US dollar buying done before Thanksgiving."

While Anthropic is seen as a bellwether for the future of AI, the boom in the technology has already influenced Wall Street's long-term dollar forecasts. Barclays Plc, Deutsche Bank AG and Standard Chartered Bank expect the dollar to extend its rally into 2027, citing US dominance in AI and its potential to lift productivity and interest rates. Anthropic's listing adds to the appeal of the US equity market and positions the company to become one of the world's most important stocks in the space.

Foreign inflows into US stocks jumped 43% to $670 billion in the January-September period, the highest since at least 2016, according to data from the Department of the Treasury compiled by Bloomberg.
The dollar gauge is up more than 3% this year, strengthening against most of its major peers.

Nomura strategist Dominic Bunning said the world's reserve currency is benefiting from other sources of support this week. Treasury yields near recent highs are keeping carry trades in the dollar's favor, Bunning added. The US 10-year yield is poised for its longest stretch above 5% since 2007.

Meanwhile, Wednesday's Fed minutes from its latest meeting showed nearly all officials agreed the central bank would likely need to raise rates "in the months ahead" to return inflation to their 2% target in a timely manner. And concerns that violence in the Middle East could escalate added to inflation worries and lifted oil prices.

"This week's been all about de-risking," said Alex Cohen, a strategist at Bank of America Corp. "US data and Fed speakers have delivered a message that further rate hikes are coming and justified. That's a good mix for the US dollar."
